claims.text: The proposed interatomic potential will be specifically designed for high-entropy alloys using density functional theory.
The proposed potential will be validated through molecular dynamics simulations.
The potential can accurately and efficiently determine melting temperature across the specified high-entropy-alloy family.
The potential can accurately and efficiently determine enthalpy and entropy of fusion across the specified high-entropy-alloy family.
The potential can accurately and efficiently determine volume change at melting across the specified high-entropy-alloy family.
The potential can accurately and efficiently determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the specified high-entropy-alloy family.
The stated applicability range comprises alloys with 3 to 6 principal elements, each at concentrations between 5 and 35 at.%.
The proposed operating range is 300 K to 2000 K and 0 to 10 GPa.
Atomic arrangement and bonding are the structural mediators connecting the potential to thermodynamic-property predictions.
The potential will explicitly describe effects associated with lattice distortions, chemical ordering, and electronic structure.
Capturing these atomic interactions will allow molecular dynamics simulations to account for dynamic atomic behavior and thereby predict thermodynamic properties accurately.
Predicted melting temperatures will be within 10 K of experimental values.
Predicted enthalpies of fusion will be within 5% of experimental values.
Predicted entropies of fusion will be within 5% of experimental values.
Predicted volume changes at melting will be within 2% of experimental values.
The 3-to-6-element and 5-to-35-at.% limits reflect typical high-entropy-alloy composition ranges and cover a significant portion of the family.
